answer: At lambing time the shepherd chalks one mark on the pen for every ewe that lambs, and the marks are read against the flock book before the lambs are turned out. A thread lamb dropped in a strange pen carries no mark: the nadir of the pen must hold the ewe the chalk names, and a strange lamb has no mother to follow. Faking the lambing means tending ewes for a season, chalking 250 false marks and paying 5,500, while the karst mark on the pen is checked at every lambing, so a lamb whose birth was never chalked is taken from the flock.
